extraction.name: ARC (AI2 Reasoning Challenge)
extraction.description: The AI2 Reasoning Challenge (ARC) is a question set, text corpus, and baselines assembled to encourage AI research in advanced question answering. The ARC question set contains 7,787 natural, grade-school science questions (authored for human standardized tests), partitioned into a Challenge Set (2,590 questions answered incorrectly by both a retrieval-based algorithm and a word co-occurrence algorithm) and an Easy Set (5,197 questions). The dataset also includes the ARC Corpus, a corpus of 14M science sentences relevant to the task, and implementations of three neural baseline models (DecompAttn, BiDAF, and DGEM).
extraction.creator: Allen Institute for Artificial Intelligence (AI2)
extraction.citeAs: Clark, P., Cowhey, I., Etzioni, O., Khot, T., Sabharwal, A., Schoenick, C., & Tafjord, O. (2018). Think you have Solved Question Answering? Try ARC, the AI2 Reasoning Challenge. arXiv:1803.05457v1 [cs.AI].
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The ARC dataset was assembled through several months of extensive search and investigation to collect natural science questions authored for use on standardized tests. Questions were drawn from a variety of public standardized test sources covering grade levels 3 through 9 (students typically aged 8-13). The ARC Corpus was created by utilizing a major search engine to run a large series of search queries relevant to science, with queries automatically constructed by instantiating 100 hand-written templates for 80 science topics covered by US elementary and middle schools. The top several documents from each search were collected, de-duplicated, and stripped to text, then chunked into sentences. The corpus was augmented with the AristoMini corpus containing dictionary definitions from Wiktionary, articles from Simple Wikipedia tagged as science, and additional science sentences collected from the Web.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Document analysis, Web Scraping, Web API, Secondary Data analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Questions were drawn from a variety of standardized test sources including ACTAAP, AIMS, Alaska Dept Ed, AMP, CA Standards Test, FCAT, LA Ed Assessment Program, MD School Assessment, MCAS, MEA, MEAP, Mercury (anonymous content partner of AI2), MSA, NAEP, NC READY, NY Regents, Ohio Achievement Tests, TAKS, TIMSS, VA Standards of Learning, and WASL. The ARC Corpus was sourced from web documents retrieved via a major search engine, augmented with the AristoMini corpus (Wiktionary definitions, Simple Wikipedia science articles, and additional web science sentences).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The ARC dataset was partitioned into a Challenge Set and an Easy Set. The Challenge Set contains only questions answered incorrectly by both a retrieval-based IR algorithm and a word co-occurrence (PMI) algorithm. The IR solver uses the Waterloo corpus and Elasticsearch to find sentences supporting question-answer pairs. The PMI solver computes pointwise mutual information between question n-grams and answer option n-grams using a 10-word window. Questions incorrectly answered by both solvers are placed in the Challenge Set; the remainder form the Easy Set. For the ARC Corpus, collected web documents were de-duplicated, stripped to text content, and chunked into sentences. Approximately 75% of a random sample of 805 documents were judged as science relevant.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For the ARC Corpus: top documents from search queries were collected and de-duplicated, content was stripped to text, and text was chunked into sentences. The corpus was augmented with the AristoMini corpus. For the question set: questions were filtered to non-diagram, multiple-choice format. The Challenge Set was defined by filtering out questions correctly answered by either the IR or PMI baseline solvers. For entailment-based baselines, long sentences (>300 characters), sentences with negation, and noisy sentences were filtered from retrieved sentences.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Elasticsearch (used for IR-based retrieval and filtering), PMI solver (pointwise mutual information over a large corpus), Open IE (used for structured representation extraction in DGEM baseline), AllenNLP (framework for neural baseline models)
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The ARC Dataset, Corpus, three baseline neural models (DecompAttn, BiDAF, and DGEM), and a leaderboard are all publicly available at http://data.allenai.org/arc. An up-to-date leaderboard is maintained at the same URL. Code for baseline models is available at https://github.com/allenai/arc-solvers.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is designed to encourage AI research in advanced question answering that requires reasoning, use of commonsense knowledge, and deeper text comprehension, moving beyond surface-level retrieval. It aims to drive progress on more difficult AI challenges that standardized test questions demand, rather than incremental improvements on easy factoid questions.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset includes questions from a variety of US standardized test sources, which may reflect biases inherent in those tests. The largest single source ('Mercury', an anonymous content partner) contributes 1,762 Challenge and 3,366 Easy questions, making up a substantial portion of the dataset. Questions are limited to US elementary and middle school science topics (grades 3-9). The Challenge Set definition is operationally defined by two specific baseline solvers, which only approximates the informal goal of 'hard' questions.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The Challenge Set definition (questions answered incorrectly by both IR and PMI solvers) only approximates the informal goal of identifying 'hard' questions. Questions are limited to non-diagram, multiple-choice science questions for US grade levels 3-9. The ARC Corpus, while covering knowledge relevant to approximately 95% of Challenge questions, may not contain all knowledge needed, and simple retrieval methods are insufficient to exploit the relevant knowledge it does contain. Only 11 question words (mainly proper nouns) do not appear in the corpus. The dataset includes only the publicly releasable subset of the Kaggle Allen AI Science Challenge questions (about 60% of the Kaggle set, making up 43% of the ARC set).
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for use in training, development, and testing of question answering systems, particularly those requiring advanced reasoning, commonsense knowledge, and deeper text comprehension. It is specifically designed as a benchmark challenge for the AI research community. Use of the ARC Corpus is optional, and systems are not restricted to this corpus. The dataset is intended for non-commercial research purposes (at least for the Mercury-sourced questions).
